vectors.name: always-on request attachment compatibility > converts legacy input added at initialization before transport validation
vectors.spec: /spec/1.0/basic/versioning#retired-shapes (DEPRECATIONS.md: {type: binary} input content part -> the media parts with a source; the always-on boundary converts it on requests AND response events)

Stated inbound: the boundary upgrades RUN_STARTED.input.messages with the same upgradeMessageContent helper. Expected content: [{type: image, source}] (no metadata: the legacy part had no filename).

vectors.name: shared legacy attachment conversion > warns and preserves an id-only attachment that cannot be converted
vectors.spec: /spec/1.0/basic/processing#what-a-consumer-does-with-unrecognised-material: inside a list, an unrecognised element is dropped and the list survives
vectors.notes: TS calls the helper directly and asserts it RETURNS the id-only binary part unchanged and warns naming 'asset-1' and DEPRECATIONS.md. Through the full pipeline the unconverted part then reaches enforcement as an unrecognised union member and is STRIPPED from the content list (TS warns "Removed unrecognised material at '/messages/0/content/0'"), so the delivered content is []. The vector pins that pipeline outcome.

vectors.name: shared legacy attachment conversion > still rejects malformed legacy payloads before transport
vectors.spec: /spec/1.0/basic/versioning#downgrading: a shim MUST NOT repair a malformed value on the way past
vectors.notes: TS asserts the OUTGOING request (onRunInitialized adds the legacy message, the transport validates it). Stated inbound: the boundary upgrades RUN_STARTED.input.messages with the same upgradeMessageContent helper. TS asserts a bare rejects.toThrow(). The boundary converts {data: 42} into an image whose source value is 42 (it does not repair it) and enforcement rejects that. Rejected by ENFORCEMENT on the canonical order (a zod message in TS, not portable), so the fragment is empty: any ProtocolError.
